idiom_name: interface in a contracts assembly + DI registration
implementation_notes: The interface keyword is a first-class contract and the implementation normally lives in another assembly, so the contract assembly can be referenced by clients while the implementation assembly is referenced only by the composition root. The container binds the two (AddSingleton<IMessageWriter, MessageWriter>()) and implementations are conventionally internal sealed so client code cannot reach them. Hand-written factory methods returning the interface remain the right form when no DI container is in play.
pitfalls: Registering the concrete type instead of the interface (or omitting the registration) fails at resolve time, not at compile time.
A scoped service captured by a singleton produces a captive-dependency lifetime bug that only appears under load.
Members implemented implicitly become public API of the class; use explicit interface implementation when the implementation type must stay internal.
